The BLAPL has been filed under Section 439, Cr.P.C.
seeking release on bail by the petitioner, who is in jail custody in connection with Nilagiri P.S.Case No.135 of 2003 corresponding to S.T.Case No.52 of 2004 pending in the court of the learned Ad hoc Additional Sessions Judge (FTSC), Balasore, for alleged commission of offence under Section 376(g)
of the I.P.C.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In response to the order dated 22.09.2023 and 13.10.2023 report has been furnished by the learned Sessions Judge.
In the report dated 18.10.2023 by letter no.425 from the Ad hoc Additional District and Sessions Judge (Fast Track Special Court) Blasore, the following has been stated :

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge (Fast Track Special Court) Blasore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: "In this regard, it is most humbly submitted that direction of the Hon'ble court in order no.02 dated 22.09.2023 in BLAPL No.9439 of 2023 was complied and the report was submitted to the Hon'ble court by E-mail in letter no.400 dated 03.10.2023.
Further, it is most humbly stated that out of 18 witnesses only three witnesses remain to be examined.

The three witnesses who are to be // 2 // examined are victim-informant, the doctor who has examined one of the accused persons and the I.O.

The victim who is also the informant belong sto the District of Bhadrak.
In spite of repeated summons and V.H.F. message her presence could not be procured.
Again V.H.F. message has been sent to IIC, Bhadrak (Rural) with copy to S.P. Bhadrak, to procure the attendance of the Victim and produce her before this Court.
Summons have been sent to the doctor for his evidence on the next date.
The case is posted to 14.11.2023 for further hearing.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was granted bail by the court in seisin of the matter, on certain dates, he did not appear before the court and thereafter he has been arrested and now is in custody.
The reasons of rejection have been stated in the order dated 22.07.2023 of the Ad hoc Additional Sessions Judge is that pursuant to the execution of NBW, the petitioner was arrested on 22.07.2023.
However, the order does not indicate that after his arrest what steps were to be taken for his examination and/or cross-examination.
4. Learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State referring to the materials on record opposes the prayer for bail.
However, it is not disputed that the trial has progressed substantially, out of 18 witnesses only three witnesses are yet to be examined.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner shall abide by stringent condition that would be imposed for grant of bail, he being rooted in the society and a local person shall not escape the jurisdiction of the learned court in seisin of the matter and co-operate in trial proceedings.

Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the State, this Court is inclined to grant bail to the petitioner subject to the stringent conditions that would be imposed by the learned court in seisin of the matter along with condition that violation of any terms and conditions that would be imposed for grant of bail, shall result in filing of the application by the law investigating agency/informant/victim for cancellation of bail.
7. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
( M.S.Sahoo) Judge Gs Kala @ Narayan Singh vs State Of Odisha ....
